subject: Startups
title: Firing Fast
description: A micro-lesson that makes Firing Fast usable.

hook.text: The hardest lesson in startups: when you know someone isn't working out, the right time to act was two weeks ago.

buildup.text: Founders delay firing because it feels cruel. But keeping a bad hire hurts the team more than letting them go.

discovery.text: Ben Horowitz calls it 'the right kind of ambition': protecting the team's mission over any individual's feelings.

twist.text: Most founders who finally fire a poor performer say: 'I should have done this months ago.' The team usually agrees.

climax.text: Fire with respect and speed: clear reasons, fair severance, and no public drama. The team is always watching.

punchline.text: Hire slow, fire fast. The team depends on it.

quiz.question: What do most founders say after firing a poor performer?
options: 'I should have done this months ago'
'We should have given them more time'
